# Known edges for the slop fixer's dash rule: a phrase after "the" that
# reads like a clause, and a clause that reads like a phrase. Each line is a
# probe; the "=> " line under it is the fix it must give, and a "~> " line
# is the fix it should give but does not yet, a known gap. A typed \u2014 is
# a dash and a typed \n a line break. Check after any rule change:
#   node scripts/slop-fix-diff.js --probe-file test/fixtures/slop-fix-edges.txt

# a clause: "the" or "its", a noun, a verb, an object
We fixed it \u2014 the loop kicks work.
=> We fixed it; the loop kicks work.
We fixed it \u2014 the gate checks the drafts.
=> We fixed it; the gate checks the drafts.
We fixed it \u2014 the hook reads `MISSION.md`.
=> We fixed it; the hook reads `MISSION.md`.
We fixed it \u2014 the gate also checks drafts.
=> We fixed it; the gate also checks drafts.
Open the panel \u2014 the user settings\npage is gone.
=> Open the panel; the user settings\npage is gone.

The site is not naive \u2014 its pages score 67.
=> The site is not naive; its pages score 67.
We fixed it \u2014 the loop kicks\nwork into the queue.
=> We fixed it; the loop kicks\nwork into the queue.
Check it \u2014 the error logs show it.
=> Check it; the error logs show it.

# a phrase: a word in s that names a thing, not a verb
Check one place \u2014 the error logs folder.
=> Check one place, the error logs folder.
Command tests \u2014 the decision helpers the CLI uses.
=> Command tests, the decision helpers the CLI uses.
Imports at module top \u2014 the stubs in tests `monkeypatch`.
=> Imports at module top, the stubs in tests `monkeypatch`.
One place \u2014 their docs folder the team uses.
=> One place, their docs folder the team uses.
One place \u2014 the error logs folder for each repo.
=> One place, the error logs folder for each repo.
The backlog \u2014 the pull requests queue for review.
=> The backlog, the pull requests queue for review.
Check it \u2014 the unit tests pass.
=> Check it; the unit tests pass.
Check it \u2014 the error logs from CI.
=> Check it, the error logs from CI.

# one word before the dash is a label, not a sentence
Then \u2014 the loop kicks work.
=> Then, the loop kicks work.

# from real repo text: "the", one noun, a verb in s, then an object of two
# or more words is a clause; "-ers" before "the", a word and a verb, a
# "that" after the verb word, or a number before it make a phrase instead
Never run git \u2014 the orchestrator lands your work.
=> Never run git; the orchestrator lands your work.
The params are client-side only \u2014 the server returns the same SSR payload.
=> The params are client-side only; the server returns the same SSR payload.
It ships without the strip \u2014 the test proves the fix works.
=> It ships without the strip; the test proves the fix works.
Dead numbers \u2014 the machine filters all of that out.
=> Dead numbers; the machine filters all of that out.
We kept the memory \u2014 the fix inlines a sync per emission.
=> We kept the memory; the fix inlines a sync per emission.
Smoke test \u2014 the phone calls the user.
=> Smoke test: the phone calls the user.
Inside the template \u2014 the system prompts that every app inherits.
=> Inside the template, the system prompts that every app inherits.
All closed \u2014 the three ways a first run could waste itself.
=> All closed, the three ways a first run could waste itself.

# from real repo text: a two-word subject ("the RL policy", "the rendering
# library") reads the same as one noun; an object of "the", up to three
# words and a verb in s after it still makes a phrase, and so does a "that"
# after the first word
It answers "which examples are useful" \u2014 the RL policy learns this automatically.
=> It answers "which examples are useful"; the RL policy learns this automatically.
Off now means off \u2014 the overnight loop stops the moment you flip the switch.
=> Off now means off; the overnight loop stops the moment you flip the switch.
It reads one store \u2014 the rendering library wraps a single `usePulseStream` and fans state out.
=> It reads one store; the rendering library wraps a single `usePulseStream` and fans state out.
The core \u2014 the block pipeline prompts the CLI uses.
=> The core, the block pipeline prompts the CLI uses.
Author block documents \u2014 the live markdown docs the Atris (obelisk) editor renders, with charts.
=> Author block documents, the live markdown docs the Atris (obelisk) editor renders, with charts.
Quality drops \u2014 the texture that makes the analysis read well needs Opus.
~> Quality drops; the texture that makes the analysis read well needs Opus.

# from real repo text: a verb in s, then "across", "through", "into" and
# kin is a clause; a plural that is almost never a verb keeps the phrase
Spread out \u2014 the protocol spreads across projects.
=> Spread out; the protocol spreads across projects.
No regex \u2014 the embedding router learns from new patterns.
=> No regex; the embedding router learns from new patterns.
Three cells \u2014 the cell silently splits into two columns.
=> Three cells; the cell silently splits into two columns.
One trick \u2014 the test cases across repos.
=> One trick, the test cases across repos.

# from real repo text: a verb in s and a bare object of two to four plain
# words or a number before a stop or comma is a clause; a longer name
# with no verb keeps the phrase
Local search first \u2014 the post claims 99% token reduction.
=> Local search first: the post claims 99% token reduction.
Reverse the curve \u2014 the scorer tracks signal quality, not order or noise.
=> Reverse the curve; the scorer tracks signal quality, not order or noise.
Same as before \u2014 the feature flags service config.
=> Same as before, the feature flags service config.
# a word in s and at most one more word before a name word and a stop is
# one long name, not a verb and its object
One place \u2014 the agent runs dashboard view.
=> One place, the agent runs dashboard view.
One place \u2014 the team calls schedule.
=> One place, the team calls schedule.

# from real repo text: before "in", "on", "to", "for", "at" or "with" only a
# verb that is almost never a plural noun makes a clause
A click is not enough \u2014 the canvas listens for a full pointer event chain.
=> A click is not enough; the canvas listens for a full pointer event chain.
The value is still empty \u2014 the field fills in only after that step finishes.
=> The value is still empty; the field fills in only after that step finishes.
Check one place \u2014 the open issues on GitHub.
=> Check one place, the open issues on GitHub.
Check one place \u2014 the GPU clusters in us-east.
=> Check one place, the GPU clusters in us-east.

# from real repo text: a field's short value before a dash and a "the"
# clause joins with a semicolon, as a pronoun clause does
Top blocker: friction_points \u2014 the known failure modes are undocumented, so the agent fails.
=> Top blocker: friction_points; the known failure modes are undocumented, so the agent fails.
Bottleneck: unchanged \u2014 the trust-playbook GO stays closed on all five dimensions.
=> Bottleneck: unchanged; the trust-playbook GO stays closed on all five dimensions.
# a value that opens on "not" takes a colon alone, but past a field's own
# colon it takes a semicolon, so no second colon stacks on it
Status: not ready \u2014 the gate holds the drafts.
=> Status: not ready; the gate holds the drafts.

# from real repo text: a verb in s with a tail that says how, not what
Irreversible by definition \u2014 the engine blocks regardless of context.
=> Irreversible by definition; the engine blocks regardless of context.
No retries here \u2014 the runner catches instead of propagating.
=> No retries here; the runner catches instead of propagating.
The result key is empty \u2014 the widget computes client-side.
=> The result key is empty; the widget computes client-side.
Check one place \u2014 the unit tests instead of mocking.
=> Check one place, the unit tests instead of mocking.
Check one place \u2014 the error logs instead of the console.
=> Check one place, the error logs instead of the console.
# a noun before a plural reads like a subject and its verb
Two views \u2014 the admin panels server-side.
~> Two views, the admin panels server-side.

# from real repo text: two verbs in s joined by "and", the second one shown
# to be a verb by an object, a how tail or a helper verb in its place
So no new parsing code \u2014 the app captures stdout and writes the file.
=> So no new parsing code; the app captures stdout and writes the file.
No latency impact \u2014 the tracing client buffers and uploads out-of-band.
=> No latency impact; the tracing client buffers and uploads out-of-band.
The row is stale \u2014 the migration shows as applied and is skipped.
=> The row is stale; the migration shows as applied and is skipped.
Check one place \u2014 the error logs and traces folder.
=> Check one place, the error logs and traces folder.

# from real repo text: a "the" inside the clause after a plural starts an
# object, so the line is a clause, not a plural with a clause on it
It mirrors what the model produces \u2014 the learner watches the model do the reps.
=> It mirrors what the model produces; the learner watches the model do the reps.
One place \u2014 the live markdown docs the Atris editor renders.
=> One place, the live markdown docs the Atris editor renders.

# from real repo text: a "what" clause or a quote after a verb in s is its
# object; a verb that is often a noun keeps the phrase before a quote
It is local for business \u2014 the business owns what its agents learn, not the lab.
=> It is local for business; the business owns what its agents learn, not the lab.
All tests pass \u2014 the verdict reads "Human decision needed."
=> All tests pass; the verdict reads "Human decision needed."
Check one place \u2014 the field names "id" and "name".
=> Check one place, the field names "id" and "name".
One place \u2014 the server logs "error" lines.
=> One place, the server logs "error" lines.
# "names" takes one quoted name in capitals as its object
note: caution \u2014 the verbatim quote names "Dave," not the owner Eric.
=> note: caution; the verbatim quote names "Dave," not the owner Eric.
# but after a word that names a thing in code or a field it stays a phrase
The schema is simple here \u2014 the field names "Id" and nothing else.
=> The schema is simple here, the field names "Id" and nothing else.
Look at the component file \u2014 the class names "Button" for the theme.
=> Look at the component file, the class names "Button" for the theme.

# from real repo text: a verb in s, a few words and "but" with a second
# clause or verb; "but not" and "but the" with no verb set two things side
# by side
Partly fixed \u2014 the lead capture works but the follow-up routing is broken.
=> Partly fixed; the lead capture works but the follow-up routing is broken.
Read it twice \u2014 the route looks like it logs backend errors but doesn't.
=> Read it twice; the route looks like it logs backend errors but doesn't.
Check one place \u2014 the error logs but not the traces.
=> Check one place, the error logs but not the traces.
Check one place \u2014 the user stories but the epics too.
=> Check one place, the user stories but the epics too.

# from real repo text: a pronoun or a code name with a place word after it
# is the verb's object
Enforced at sandbox level \u2014 the subprocess restricts `__import__` to only these modules.
=> Enforced at sandbox level; the subprocess restricts `__import__` to only these modules.
No direct calls beyond the list \u2014 the dashboard component drives everything else.
=> No direct calls beyond the list; the dashboard component drives everything else.
"Describe who you need \u2014 the orchestrator drafts it"
=> "Describe who you need; the orchestrator drafts it"
# "yes" after a pronoun ends in s but is no second verb
Wondering "did Hugo reply?" \u2014 the tag tells you yes/no instantly without searching.
=> Wondering "did Hugo reply?"; the tag tells you yes/no instantly without searching.
# a two-word label before the dash is no clause, so a colon reads better
LLM psychosis \u2014 every AI validates you, agrees with you.
=> LLM psychosis: every AI validates you, agrees with you.
# but a colon at the end of the same sentence would stack, so it stays
Joint pool \u2014 the whole story is in three rows:
=> Joint pool; the whole story is in three rows:
# and words after a list label's own colon open no line
- `list_runs()` \u2014 line 134 \u2014 the runs come back newest first.
=> - `list_runs()`: line 134; the runs come back newest first.
# a past verb with a prefix and a bare plural before a place word is a clause
It only passed that week \u2014 the card re-filtered orders against today's date.
=> It only passed that week; the card re-filtered orders against today's date.
# but "in" after the plural can still close a noun phrase
We kept them \u2014 the auto generated files in the repo.
=> We kept them, the auto generated files in the repo.
# a bare plural with its own "that" clause after the verb is an object
Both count as satisfying \u2014 the spread branch covers routes that merge in extra headers.
=> Both count as satisfying; the spread branch covers routes that merge in extra headers.
# but a common plural noun is no verb, so the phrase keeps its comma
Open the panel \u2014 the user settings pages that load slowly.
=> Open the panel, the user settings pages that load slowly.
# "the", a word with no s, a plural and a common verb with more words is a clause
Title comes from the alt text \u2014 the text title elements use obfuscated class names.
=> Title comes from the alt text; the text title elements use obfuscated class names.
We ranked them \u2014 the 4 candidates cluster on unrelated concerns.
=> We ranked them; the 4 candidates cluster on unrelated concerns.
# a verb that is almost never a noun takes "from" or "as" after it, and "their" can open it
The ideas page is a React app \u2014 their visible data comes from the APIs above.
=> The ideas page is a React app; their visible data comes from the APIs above.
It turns a wish into daily process \u2014 the wish arrives as a byproduct.
=> It turns a wish into daily process; the wish arrives as a byproduct.
# a word in "ly" right before a past verb makes it a verb
No hand-wavy guesses \u2014 the miss patterns directly pointed to each change.
=> No hand-wavy guesses; the miss patterns directly pointed to each change.
# but a number before it is a count with its own phrase
It fixed 18 features \u2014 the 10 directly edited plus 8 that moved.
=> It fixed 18 features, the 10 directly edited plus 8 that moved.
# a closing quote ends a bare object of two to four words
The claim "closes the loop with the gate work \u2014 the classifier reads real outcome data" is withdrawn.
=> The claim "closes the loop with the gate work; the classifier reads real outcome data" is withdrawn.
# but a plural noun where the verb would be keeps the phrase
He wrote "start with one screen \u2014 the user settings page layout" in the doc.
=> He wrote "start with one screen, the user settings page layout" in the doc.
# a wrapped clause inside a quote reads on into the next line at the same depth
> Pass the brain context as part of the prompt \u2014 the web search focuses on\n> the delta between brain knowledge and web state.
=> > Pass the brain context as part of the prompt; the web search focuses on\n> the delta between brain knowledge and web state.
# but a quote one level up is no wrap
>> Keep the whole note short \u2014 the web search focuses on\n> the delta between them.
=> >> Keep the whole note short, the web search focuses on\n> the delta between them.
# a code name with an underscore is one word before the subject noun
No placeholder logic here \u2014 the business_id match handles the bypass class codex flagged.
=> No placeholder logic here; the business_id match handles the bypass class codex flagged.
# but with no verb after it the phrase keeps its comma
Two tables matter here \u2014 the business_id lookups and the agent rows.
=> Two tables matter here, the business_id lookups and the agent rows.
# "that's" after an "if" clause's comma opens a main clause, as "that is" does
Track the pass rate over time \u2014 if variance is high, that's the signal.
=> Track the pass rate over time; if variance is high, that's the signal.
# but with no subject after the comma the clause only adds a condition
Ship the whole thing soon \u2014 if you can, today.
=> Ship the whole thing soon, if you can, today.
# "which", a noun and a helper verb after a verb in s is its object
Check the checklist by hand \u2014 the web UI shows exactly which item has the yellow dot.
=> Check the checklist by hand; the web UI shows exactly which item has the yellow dot.
# but "which" with a verb right after it opens a clause inside the phrase
Skip the noise for now \u2014 the error logs which show results.
=> Skip the noise for now, the error logs which show results.
# "yes" is no plural, and a possessive in capitals opens an object
People-pleasing looks kind from outside \u2014 the fake yes buys YOUR comfort with counterfeit commitment.
=> People-pleasing looks kind from outside; the fake yes buys YOUR comfort with counterfeit commitment.
# but with no verb after it the phrase keeps its comma
The vote split two ways \u2014 the yes side and the no side.
=> The vote split two ways, the yes side and the no side.
# a possessive inside a past verb phrase opens a new noun, so the phrase keeps its comma
Look at the column first \u2014 the tests YOUR team wrote.
=> Look at the column first, the tests YOUR team wrote.
He watched her read the page \u2014 the way her eyes moved.
=> He watched her read the page, the way her eyes moved.
# a dash pressed against a hyphenated word after a parenthesis or a space is a flag's two hyphens
Hook alone is not enough (\u2014no-verify can bypass it); tests catch it.
=> Hook alone is not enough (--no-verify can bypass it); tests catch it.
Run git commit \u2014no-verify to skip the hook.
=> Run git commit --no-verify to skip the hook.
# a short aside that ends on the word before its dash says it again, so it takes commas
Follow your curiosity even when \u2014 especially when \u2014 it has no use.
=> Follow your curiosity even when, especially when, it has no use.
We need the best \u2014 maybe the only \u2014 way out.
=> We need the best (maybe the only) way out.
# a closing double brace of a template slot ends a clause like a word
Smaller on {{WEAKEST}} \u2014 that's the next round.
=> Smaller on {{WEAKEST}}; that's the next round.
# "most" or "least" before an "ed" word starts a noun phrase, not a clause
Our plan is set \u2014 the most requested features from users.
=> Our plan is set, the most requested features from users.
We looked again \u2014 the best part comes from the tests.
=> We looked again; the best part comes from the tests.
# a one-word object before "when" or "before" ends a clause, as before "to"
Dedup is a prerequisite \u2014 the score function breaks down when the pool fills.
=> Dedup is a prerequisite; the score function breaks down when the pool fills.
One gap \u2014 the admin tools menu before login.
=> One gap, the admin tools menu before login.
# a one-word object before "and" and a second verb ends a clause, as before "or"
It has no baseline \u2014 this experiment creates one and optimizes it.
=> It has no baseline; this experiment creates one and optimizes it.
Two screens left \u2014 the user reports page and exports tab.
=> Two screens left, the user reports page and exports tab.
# "this" plus "directly" or "silently" plus a verb is a clause, like "this still"
The services have no compression \u2014 this directly caps session quality.
=> The services have no compression; this directly caps session quality.
We read the weekly digest \u2014 this weekly reports page.
=> We read the weekly digest, this weekly reports page.
# up to three bare words before "which" or "that" and a verb end a clause; "analysis" is no verb
It is weak \u2014 the current implementation uses simple keyword matching which has obvious gaps.
=> It is weak; the current implementation uses simple keyword matching which has obvious gaps.
TARGET: `target.py` \u2014 a dependency analysis function that takes a list of calls.
=> TARGET: `target.py`, a dependency analysis function that takes a list of calls.
# two short clauses that repeat one verb spell out the words before the dash, so a colon
This reframes the goal as credit savings \u2014 a false promotion costs 3 credits, a false quick costs quality.
=> This reframes the goal as credit savings: a false promotion costs 3 credits, a false quick costs quality.
We count both \u2014 a miss costs a day, a false alarm wastes an hour.
=> We count both; a miss costs a day, a false alarm wastes an hour.
The old scorers are spent at their current design \u2014 those need redesigns, not more runs.
=> The old scorers are spent at their current design; those need redesigns, not more runs.
Based on the full picture \u2014 7 at ceiling (1.0), 5 broken \u2014 the daemon has nothing to run.
=> Based on the full picture (7 at ceiling [1.0], 5 broken), the daemon has nothing to run.
Looking at the stalls \u2014 the scorer flat at 0.9, the config stuck \u2014 the loop needs new targets.
=> Looking at the stalls (the scorer flat at 0.9, the config stuck), the loop needs new targets.
Two picks \u2014 (1) the loop, and (2) the community \u2014 keep people.
=> Two picks, (1) the loop, and (2) the community, keep people.
The bottleneck is the plan step \u2014 a miscalibrated DECIDE wastes every later cycle.
=> The bottleneck is the plan step; a miscalibrated DECIDE wastes every later cycle.
Two tools \u2014 the API keys the team uses and the bot.
=> Two tools, the API keys the team uses and the bot.
False alarms cost trust. Estimated baseline ~78% \u2014 the edge cases around file reads and partial sends are handled badly.
=> False alarms cost trust. Estimated baseline ~78%; the edge cases around file reads and partial sends are handled badly.
Parse failures drop tool calls \u2014 the agent thinks it completed but nothing happened.
=> Parse failures drop tool calls; the agent thinks it completed but nothing happened.
Two builds \u2014 the new build signed but not shipped, and the old one.
=> Two builds, the new build signed but not shipped, and the old one.
_Dropped: Nothing \u2014 the source returned no posts to filter._
=> _Dropped: Nothing; the source returned no posts to filter._
Result: 0 trainable / 0 dead \u2014 every task passed all 5 samples.
=> Result: 0 trainable / 0 dead; every task passed all 5 samples.
A falsifier for "why is it silent?" \u2014 each layer narrowed the hypothesis space.
=> A falsifier for "why is it silent?"; each layer narrowed the hypothesis space.
Built with care \u2014 every claim measured, not asserted.
=> Built with care, every claim measured, not asserted.
The scanner runs on every diff \u2014 if its F1 is below 0.95, that's a real gap.
=> The scanner runs on every diff; if its F1 is below 0.95, that's a real gap.
It ran \u2014 if the score is 0.9. Then we ship.
=> It ran, if the score is 0.9. Then we ship.
The contract has a test on both sides \u2014 if the format changes, the round-trip test fails and we catch it.
=> The contract has a test on both sides; if the format changes, the round-trip test fails and we catch it.
The contract has a test on both sides \u2014 if the format changes, the test results and the logs go to S3.
=> The contract has a test on both sides, if the format changes, the test results and the logs go to S3.

# after an "if" clause, a verb in "s", "and the" and a second verb in "s"
# is two clauses, but "the test results and the team logs in tests" reads
# the same and is a noun list; no real line in the corpus has it yet
The gate has a test \u2014 if the format changes, the round-trip check breaks and the team reverts it.
~> The gate has a test; if the format changes, the round-trip check breaks and the team reverts it.

# a subject of two nouns joined by "and its" before a plural verb, from a
# real goal repeated across one repo's logs, with "feel as trustworthy as"
# for its verb; two nouns with no verb after them stay a phrase
Nobody has to leave Atris while working \u2014 the in-app browser and its file-viewing companions (PDF, HTML) feel as trustworthy as a real browser tab.
=> Nobody has to leave Atris while working; the in-app browser and its file-viewing companions (PDF, HTML) feel as trustworthy as a real browser tab.
Nobody leaves Atris \u2014 the browser and its companions show the page.
=> Nobody leaves Atris; the browser and its companions show the page.
Nobody leaves Atris \u2014 the file viewers feel as safe as a tab.
=> Nobody leaves Atris; the file viewers feel as safe as a tab.
Check one place \u2014 the logs and the docs folder.
=> Check one place, the logs and the docs folder.

# a short aside between the subject and its verb is read past, so the
# clause joins the way it does with no aside; a phrase with an aside keeps
# its comma
We fixed it \u2014 the member definition (MEMBER.md / backend member schema) carries its model.
=> We fixed it; the member definition (MEMBER.md / backend member schema) carries its model.
We fixed it \u2014 the proof-gate contract (`gate.mjs`) bans the fake-done wording.
=> We fixed it; the proof-gate contract (`gate.mjs`) bans the fake-done wording.
Check one place \u2014 the error logs (in /tmp) folder.
=> Check one place, the error logs (in /tmp) folder.

# a bare object after the verb, with an aside before it: the check for a
# bare object reads past the aside too
The HMAC path still works \u2014 the refactor (hmac_key to auth_secret) preserves behavior.
=> The HMAC path still works; the refactor (hmac_key to auth_secret) preserves behavior.

# "these" or "those" and a verb the fixer reads since the wider list found
# them in real docs; "live" is a verb only before a place word
Two parsers \u2014 these live in the parser.
=> Two parsers; these live in the parser.
Logs are risky \u2014 these often carry request bodies.
=> Logs are risky; these often carry request bodies.
Most runs stall \u2014 these hit local optima.
=> Most runs stall; these hit local optima.
We ran demos \u2014 those live demo runs.
=> We ran demos, those live demo runs.
Check the counts \u2014 those hit rates.
=> Check the counts, those hit rates.

# "The" and a noun that only names a point is a whole sentence the clause
# spells out, so it takes a colon; a sentence with its own verb keeps the
# semicolon
Runs stall. The common thread \u2014 these hit local optima.
=> Runs stall. The common thread: these hit local optima.
The real fix \u2014 the parser drops the key.
=> The real fix: the parser drops the key.
The fix shipped \u2014 the parser drops the key.
=> The fix shipped; the parser drops the key.
We found the common thread \u2014 these hit local optima.
=> We found the common thread; these hit local optima.

# "no longer" before a verb is a clause, like "never" or "still", and a
# bare verb may sit before a comma and "so"; a word that is mostly an
# adjective there, or no verb at all, keeps the comma
We moved it \u2014 the computer page no longer swaps the chrome.
=> We moved it; the computer page no longer swaps the chrome.
The claims were false \u2014 those directories no longer exist, so they are unchecked.
=> The claims were false; those directories no longer exist, so they are unchecked.
We dropped it \u2014 the old flags no longer valid, so skip them.
=> We dropped it, the old flags no longer valid, so skip them.
We fixed it \u2014 pages no longer found.
=> We fixed it, pages no longer found.

# a noun phrase with "still" and an adjective, no verb: the plain clause
# rule reads the plural noun as a verb ("the old flags") and joins it. A
# count of this shape after a dash across the real docs found no line
# like it, so it stays a known gap rather than a guard
We dropped it \u2014 the old flags still valid for users.
~> We dropped it, the old flags still valid for users.

# "did", "hid" and "set" are past verbs after "the" and a noun, from real
# docs; "set" counts only before "it", "them" or a word like "up"
The architecture didn't change \u2014 the SCALE did.
=> The architecture didn't change; the SCALE did.
It was never a Claude failure \u2014 the label hid a codex credential gap.
=> It was never a Claude failure; the label hid a codex credential gap.
They are load-bearing context \u2014 the user set them up for a reason.
=> They are load-bearing context; the user set them up for a reason.
Clean it first \u2014 the data set a team uses.
=> Clean it first, the data set a team uses.
